# Ternuxx

**Repository:** [`soobujmiah/ternuxx`](https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx). Use ./tx from a source checkout or the installed tx command.

**বাংলা:** Pocket-এ mobile workstation তৈরির স্বাধীন project। Native Termux layer compatible tools ও Android-facing integration-এর সুযোগ দেবে; বিদ্যমান Ternux Debian PRoot layer Linux desktop, established workload ও configured GPU path দেবে। Hybrid mode দুটিকে নিরাপদ handoff দিয়ে এক workstation-এ যুক্ত করবে।

**English:** I want my phone to be a workstation I can carry in my pocket. I want native Termux and my existing Ternux PRoot setup to work together, so I can use each where it fits. Read [what I have in mind](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md).

## Planned use and current workstation boundary

- **Native mode:** Native Termux is the Ternuxx host and management authority. Its CPU is the baseline; the current Native display process reports llvmpipe and its installed Vulkan route rejects Adreno 825.
- **Debian PRoot:** Ternuxx uses the existing installed Debian rootfs directly through typed proot-distro operations. On display :1, the read-only guest check currently verifies Zink/Turnip Adreno 825 and authenticated Native PulseAudio client reachability. Full interactive attach/detach/stop ownership remains unqualified.
- **Hybrid handoff:** Ternuxx routes selected guest applications to its verified Native :1 display and host audio endpoint. VirGL remains a separate preserved option but is not active/renderer-qualified in this snapshot.

The separate Ternux project remains independent and reference-only. Ternuxx does not require its CLI or state files. Existing Debian user data, packages, GPU setup, db/launcher aliases, x.sh, xgo, and killx are preserved; any targeted guest config adaptation requires a bounded impact assessment and recovery plan. Native Bionic libraries are not copied into Debian glibc paths. NPU execution remains unverified.

## Development notes

The install command uses a preview-first Termux APT transaction and persists full dependency plans under private Ternuxx state; its approved 2026-10-18 XFCE install is recorded with all 77 package versions in P2 evidence. P2 is complete for the recorded target. P3 remains active. Ternuxx now runs its own bounded, read-only Debian display/audio/renderer verification and passes explicit Native display, cookie-authenticated PulseAudio, and Zink/Turnip settings to its direct PRoot commands; it does not invoke the separate Ternux CLI. Headless session fixtures pass, but interactive login, detach/reattach, exact live stop, production boot, and shared-rootfs concurrency remain unqualified. Native Vulkan rejects Adreno 825; the current Debian guest reports Zink/Turnip. Native GPU, VirGL renderer, inference CPU/GPU workload, and NPU runtime/workload remain unqualified.

Ternuxx itself has no implemented inference backend or benchmark; the separate Ternux repository documents optional CPU/Vulkan llama.cpp and experimental SM8735 HTP extensions whose installed state and Ternuxx integration remain unverified.

The accepted product direction has four clients—CLI, interactive Terminal/TUI, Web UI, and Native graphical UI—calling one shared management service and operation contract. ## Brand and license status

**Ternuxx** is the product and repository name. The only public command is tx (./tx in a source checkout).

This repository is public, but it has no `LICENSE` file and GitHub reports no detected license. Earlier commits stated “PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 plus the Ternux commercial-use addendum” and referenced files that were never committed. That historical statement is unresolved and needs qualified legal review. Do not treat the code as open source, assume the missing addendum's terms, or add a replacement license until the owner resolves the history and approves a license. See the [commercial and legal readiness audit](docs/readiness/README.md).


### Ternuxx Management Center

Use `tx tui` for the compact keyboard interface, `tx web` for the authenticated loopback Web Console, and `tx mng center install` followed by `tx mng center` for the separate Native Termux GTK4 application inside the existing graphical session. All three clients use the shared resource catalog and management service. The Web Console exposes catalog-backed status/diagnostics, confirmed desktop start/stop/restart, preview-confirmed start/stop for managed SSH on 8023, and the GUI Activity/focus monitoring policy. The TUI adds category navigation, search, live status reads, an advanced recovery-history view, guided native desktop and preview-confirmed managed SSH 8023 actions, PRoot app launch, and the same monitoring policy form. The GTK app provides category/search/resource details, live inspection, a recovery-history view, confirmed desktop start/stop, preview-confirmed managed SSH 8023 start/stop, and monitoring-policy configuration.

Cron definitions now have a typed, persistent registry and deterministic schedule previews under `tx mng cron`; the lease-guarded scheduler runtime is available for explicit start but is not installed in boot or started by default. Production retry, cancellation, non-skip missed-run and boot/recovery delivery remain unqualified. The management clients keep Android Activity/focus monitoring disabled by default; status reads do not launch Termux:X11 or poll Android focus. The Web listener stays loopback-only and browser writes use a one-time terminal secret, scoped capabilities, CSRF proof, confirmation, and durable idempotency. Port 8022 is read-only and externally managed; SSH deployment/rollback, boot changes, PRoot shortcut changes, general server deployment, service log browsing, and operation-progress tracking are not yet available in these clients; the shared recovery journal is available as operation history. Resource cards identify planned or unavailable work instead of simulating it. The Native GTK app is installed from repository source with a source/installed hash record. Launching it creates an X11 window and may take desktop focus.

### Managed SSH service deployment

The native managed SSH service on port 8023 has a preview-first run-definition deployment workflow. `tx ssh deploy` shows a hash-bound diff; apply requires `--yes --plan-id` from that preview. Deployment preserves the running process and never restarts the service. Snapshot rollback is also preview-first (`tx ssh deploy-rollback-preview --operation-id ID`, then `tx ssh deploy-rollback --operation-id ID --yes --plan-id PLAN`). The separate owner-started 8022 development channel is not managed by this workflow. Process ownership/reboot qualification limitations are recorded in [8023 evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-18-8023-reconciliation.md); see the [qualification plan](docs/testing/8023-deployment-and-lifecycle.md).
